metaDesc: A 1-day Suphan Buri itinerary you can drive from Bangkok: Bueng Chawak, the Banharn-Jaemsai Tower and the 100-year-old Sam Chuk Market — with real hours, entry fees and a route that never backtracks.
keywords: Suphan Buri 1 day trip, Bueng Chawak, Banharn-Jaemsai Tower, Sam Chuk Market, Suphan Buri itinerary
h1:
Suphan Buri in 1 Day
Bueng Chawak · Tower · Sam Chuk Market
intro: Suphan Buri sits only about 100–110 km from Bangkok, roughly a 1.5–2 hour drive, which makes it an easy out-and-back day trip. In a single day you can cover the three places everyone comes to Suphan for: Bueng Chawak, which is both a zoo and an aquarium; the Banharn-Jaemsai Tower in the town centre; and the century-old Sam Chuk Market on the Tha Chin River. This is the route that flows best, driving in a loop without doubling back.

blocks.html: Up front, honestly: Suphan Buri is a lot more fun with your own car, because the three main sights are in different districts. Bueng Chawak is up in Doembang Nangbuat District in the north of the province, the tower is in the town centre, and Sam Chuk falls in between. You can go without a car, but you'll be relying on several leg-by-leg songthaew rides and it eats up a lot more time. This plan is written for people driving themselves.

One more thing to know first: Bueng Chawak and Sam Chuk Market are busiest on Saturdays and Sundays. At Sam Chuk the shops are only fully open on weekends — on weekdays many are closed. If you have the choice, go on a Saturday or Sunday so you get the full atmosphere and all the food.

The heart of the plan is to hit the farthest spot first, then slowly drive back toward town so you never backtrack. Leave Bangkok in the morning, head to Bueng Chawak as your first stop in the late morning, then drop south to Sam Chuk for lunch, and finish at the tower in the town centre in the evening before driving home. Total distance within the province is about 40–50 km between stops.

items: Bangkok → Bueng Chawak — take Route 340 (Bang Bua Thong–Suphan Buri), continue past the town toward Chai Nat, about 2 hrs from Bangkok
Bueng Chawak → Sam Chuk Market — drive back south toward town, about 30–40 min
Sam Chuk Market → Banharn-Jaemsai Tower — into Suphan town centre, about 25–30 min
Tower → Bangkok — back on Route 340, about 1 hr 45 min

blocks.title: Why start at Bueng Chawak
blocks.html: Bueng Chawak is the spot where you'll walk the longest (2–3 hrs) and it's the farthest out. Going in the late morning means the sun isn't harsh yet, so it's comfortable on foot. By the afternoon you ease back toward town and finish at the tower right at golden hour, going up for the city view in nice light.

items.note: Fill up the tank and get set for a long drive. Heading out a little early helps you dodge the traffic leaving the city. There are coffee stops here and there along Route 340.

items.activity: Arrive at Bueng Chawak Chaloem Phrakiat (Doembang Nangbuat District)
items.note: Start with the aquarium building and fish tunnel first — it's cool and comfortable inside, which suits the late morning.

items.activity: Walk the aquarium + fish tunnel + undersea world zone
items.note: Entry to Buildings 1–2 and the crocodile pond is 30 THB for adults, 10 THB for kids · the Undersea World building (Building 3) is 150 THB for adults, 50 THB for kids · ages 60 and over enter free.

items.activity: Walk the zoo zone + large aviary
items.note: There are tigers, wildlife, and a walk-through aviary you can step inside. If you've brought kids, they'll love this part. If you're tired of walking, a tram runs around the lake.

items.activity: Leave Bueng Chawak, drive down to Sam Chuk
items.note: About 30–40 min, taking the road that runs toward Sam Chuk District.

items.activity: Arrive at the 100-year-old Sam Chuk Market for lunch
items.note: Park in the lot in front of the market and walk into the old wooden lanes. Hunt for food first while you're good and hungry.

Try the noodles at Jek Eh, a long-standing shop, plus roast duck and braised goose, old-style Thai sweets, and traditional coffee at Tha Ruea Song. Walk and photograph the wooden shophouses along the Tha Chin River.

items.activity: Leave Sam Chuk, head into Suphan town
items.note: About 25–30 min. On the way you can stop at Wat Pa Lelai to pay respects to Luang Pho To if you still have the energy.

Pay respects to Luang Pho To, a large Buddha in the Pa Lelai (forest-dwelling) posture in U-Thong style. It's an old temple at the heart of the town's history, free to enter, and takes about 30–40 min.

A 123-metre tower in the town centre — take the lift to the viewpoint for a 360° look over Suphan. Entry is 30 THB for adults, 15 THB for kids (before 6 pm). You can also stroll Chaloem Phatra Rachini Park at the base.
In town there are boat-noodle and fish-noodle shops, and you can pick up Suphan's salee (crispy wafer) sweets to take home.
Same Route 340, reaching Bangkok around 8 pm if there's no traffic.

blocks.title: Adjust the plan to your energy
blocks.html: If it's just a few of you and you don't want to rush, drop Wat Pa Lelai. Spend the time at Bueng Chawak and Sam Chuk instead, then hit the tower in the evening for the nice light. This plan is flexible — you don't have to follow the clock exactly.

blocks.text: Bueng Chawak — how to make it worth it

blocks.html: Bueng Chawak Chaloem Phrakiat is a large natural freshwater lake developed into a learning centre, with a zoo, an aquarium, a freshwater fish tunnel, a simulated undersea-world zone, and a crocodile pond. The entry fee is very cheap for what you get to see, which is why families love bringing kids here.

items: Opening hours — Mon–Fri 08:30–16:30 · Sat–Sun and public holidays open until 17:00
Entry fees — Buildings 1–2 + crocodile pond: adults 30 / kids 10 THB · Undersea World building: adults 150 / kids 50 THB · ages 60+ free
Highlight — the walk-through fish tunnel, both freshwater and saltwater zones, with fish swimming over your head
Time needed — an easy 2–3 hrs; there's a tram if you don't feel like walking

blocks.title: Free-entry periods
blocks.html: During some festivals and long weekends, the province runs free-entry days for Thai visitors in batches. Check the Suphan Buri provincial page before you go — if it lines up with a promotion, you'll save even more.

blocks.text: Sam Chuk Market — what to eat

blocks.html: Sam Chuk is an old market on the Tha Chin River, well over a hundred years old, with two-storey wooden shophouses lined up along a long lane. It was once a bustling waterborne trading district; now it's a walk-and-eat market with a retro feel, plenty of food, and prices in the tens of baht — perfect for a lunch stop.

items.name: Jek Eh Noodles
items.blurb: A long-standing noodle shop in the market making fresh Teochew-style noodles. It's been around a long time and is well known to anyone who visits Sam Chuk, with a well-balanced broth.
items.meta: Savoury · tens of baht per bowl

items.name: Roast Duck & Braised Goose
items.blurb: Roast duck with crispy skin and tender meat, plus braised goose from an old recipe — a signature of this area. Eat in or take it to go.

items.name: Tha Ruea Song Traditional Coffee
items.blurb: An old-style coffee shop with a vintage feel, brewing it strong and aromatic. Sip it in a wooden shophouse by the water — a good rest stop while walking the market.

items.name: Traditional Thai Sweets
items.blurb: Thong yip, thong yot, khanom buang and other sweets made fresh in the market. Buy some to snack on or take home as gifts.

items.name: Giant Fried Meatballs
items.blurb: Big meatballs on a skewer, deep-fried — a popular snack to carry around while you browse the market. Kids love them.
items.meta: Snack · tens of baht per skewer

blocks.title: Weekends have the edge
blocks.html: Sam Chuk is lively and its shops are fully open only on Saturdays and Sundays. On weekdays many shops are closed and it's much quieter. If you're coming mainly to eat and wander, a weekend is the better bet.

blocks.text: Banharn-Jaemsai Tower — finish in the evening

blocks.html: The Banharn-Jaemsai Tower stands in Chaloem Phatra Rachini Park in the centre of Suphan town. It's a viewing tower about 123 metres tall — take the lift to the observation deck for a 360° view over the city, with a shady public park below for a stroll. It's a good way to cap the trip in the evening before the light fades.

items: Opening hours — open daily except Monday · Tue–Fri 10:00–19:00 · Sat–Sun and public holidays open later
Tower entry — before 6 pm: adults 30 / kids 15 THB · after 6 pm: adults 40 / kids 20 THB
Tip — come before 6 pm to catch both the daytime view and the city lights coming on at dusk — best value

blocks.text: If you have time to spare

items.name: Wat Pa Lelai Worawihan
items.blurb: Pay respects to Luang Pho To, a large Buddha in the Pa Lelai posture in U-Thong style — an old temple central to the town, free to enter, right in town.

items.name: Dragon Descendants Museum
items.blurb: A museum tracing the history of Chinese people in Thailand. Entry is around 99 THB, near the town centre.

items.name: Boat Noodles in Town
items.blurb: Suphan is known for boat noodles and fish noodles, easy to find in town — a good dinner before you head home.

faq.q: Where should I start a 1-day trip to Suphan Buri?
faq.a: Start at Bueng Chawak, which is the farthest out and takes the longest to walk. Get there in the late morning, then slowly drive back toward town, stopping at Sam Chuk Market for lunch and finishing at the Banharn-Jaemsai Tower in the evening. That way you never backtrack and you finish right at golden hour.

faq.q: How much is entry to Bueng Chawak?
faq.a: The aquarium Buildings 1–2 plus the crocodile pond cost 30 THB for adults and 10 THB for kids. The Undersea World (Building 3) is 150 THB for adults and 50 THB for kids. Seniors aged 60 and over enter free.

faq.q: What days is Sam Chuk Market open?
faq.a: It's open daily, roughly 08:00–17:00, but the shops are fully open and the atmosphere is liveliest on Saturdays and Sundays. On weekdays many shops are closed and it's quieter, so go on a weekend if you can.

faq.q: Can I visit Suphan Buri without my own car?
faq.a: You can, but it's less convenient, because the three main sights are in different districts and you'd need to change songthaews several times. Without a car, it's best to hire a vehicle or take a day tour, or stick to the town centre where the spots are close together.

faq.q: When is the best time to go up the Banharn-Jaemsai Tower?
faq.a: Evening, before 6 pm, is the best value — you get both the daytime city view and the lights coming on at dusk. Entry before 6 pm is 30 THB for adults and 15 THB for kids. The tower is closed on Mondays.
